utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, actually today, call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Jadranko Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Madam Registrar. I would like to say good morning to all those in the courtroom, the witness who is going to complete his testimony today. So without further ado, I give the floor to Mr. Mundis, and to ask him to speed up as much as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I owe you a bit of an apology yesterday. We were at the end of the day and rushing a bit. I want to start this morning by, first of all, expressing my condolences on the loss of your wife. And I know this must be a difficult thing for you to talk about.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I apologise for that. Sir, we had left yesterday, in fact, you had just talked about, I think, the location on her body where your wife had been shot, and I believe you had indicated that the bullet entered her body in her head behind her left ear; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in a few moments we're going to be looking at some video material. I can ask you more specific questions, if need be at that time and it may be more helpful when we have the pictures in front of us. So I will skip over any more details about that in a moment. Based on everything you knew at the time and what you could observe at the time that your wife was killed on the 6th of June, 1993, can you tell the Judges where you believe the shot came from, the location that the shot came from which struck your wife?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bullet that hit my wife came from Stotina. I'm 100 per cent sure. And I can elaborate if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please do, and I will ask you to elaborate, and in doing so, let me ask you, prior to the 6th of June, 1993, had you seen any activity or positions at that location?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In that location there had been activities going on for a long time, bunkers were fortified. It was fortified with sacks and it was visible with a naked eye. I saw HVO soldiers walking around there because for a while we fought against the Serbs together. I knew many people there. They were my neighbours and after that we still exchanged jokes, we made fun together, we talked. There was a lot of activity going on. That's the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: When you say you exchanged jokes, could you actually, over the distance to Stotina, could you actually carry out voice communications, I mean, with a loud voice? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly while we were together the Brkic bridge was already destroyed, so we shouted at each other. They shouted, "You Balijas." We shouted, "You Ustashas," et cetera. And people fished at that time in Mostar, they bathed in the Neretva river. It was hot in those summer months. And we saw each other. We didn't shoot each other. My wife was the first to be hit by a sniper in that part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That was my next question to you based on what you just said. Can you tell us, prior to the 6th of June when your wife was shot, had there been any sniping activity directly against civilians in that area before?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There had been incidents where people were wounded, but nobody had been killed at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And before we continue on, can you tell the Judges as best you can remember, estimate the approximate distance between the location where your wife was shot and this position at Stotina, approximately?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 400, 420 metres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, we were listening carefully to you, and what you are saying is very important. We are finding out, because this is the first time we are hearing this, that at this position of Stotina, there were bunkers. This is the first time we hear of it. So my question is, those people that were 400 metres away from you, they were civilians or they were military troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were uniformed troops, and maybe I didn't put it very well, but at this position there were bunkers fortified with sandbags. It was a fortification with sandbags.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that from the place you were at, from your house, you saw military men in uniform. My question is, they belonged to what army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were soldiers of the HVO. The Croatian Defence Council.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did you know precisely to which unit they belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not. I know they were probably from down there in Rodoc, residents of Rodoc. I don't know what kind of deployment they had, what kind of shifts, because they had shifts, relieving each other at Hum, at Stotina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you said to the Prosecutor a moment ago that you had exchanges with them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we had verbal duels.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The only thing that we the Judges are interested in is where the bullet came from, because that is the point on which we have to decide in our judgement, where the bullet came from. So from your house, from your location, could a bullet have come from another location than Stotina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A shot could have come from Hum, but I know for sure, I know with certainty, that Opina, the Brkic bridge and the area under the cemetery where I live, Mejdan, and the Tekija Street were covered by Stotina. Whereas Hum covered an area below Razvitak company and I know that from the Glas bank in Mostar, in Zuvanica Street, another area across the Tito Bridge was targeted. I had that knowledge before my wife was killed and after my wife was killed, and obviously before and after her death I experienced a lot of things and I saw a lot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is the distance between your house and Hum, as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, maybe Hum is a hill perhaps 400 metres high, and if you draw a diagonal, it could be 100 metres, 200 metres. What could be the distance between Stotina and Hum, that is it, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You did not understand me well. From the terrace of your house, if I drew a straight line to Hum, what would be the distance between your terrace and Hum?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let's say 600 metres. I'm not an expert in these matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. At Hum, to the best of your knowledge, were there any troops?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lots of troops. At Hum there was a bunker and I watched that bunker, I saw it being blown up when it was hit. Two HVO soldiers died on that occasion. Five HVO soldiers died on that occasion, that's the information we got on this side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You told me that there was -- there were troops there and you answered my next question in advance. To what army did the troops at Hum belong, those who were approximately 600 metres away from your terrace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I could have the map, please, that the witness marked yesterday. A map was marked at the request of the President. If we could use that same map again, please. Sorry, I didn't get the IC number. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we can be of assistance. IC 296.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, counsel. It's coming up in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if you can see in front of you on the screen -- can you see a map on the screen in front of you now?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is the same map that you marked yesterday. You will see the markings. Could I ask you now - you may need the usher's assistance, please - as best you can on the map, and I realise -- well, I won't say any more. Can you just mark as best you can where the Stotina position was located as best you are able on this particular map?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stotina is exactly just above the Hasan Brkic bridge. This fly over coming in here and just above it is Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Since we now have two markings on the map, can I please ask you, the first marking in red that you made yesterday, could I ask you to mark that with a number 1?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you, please, to mark the Stotina location number 2?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You could also indicate Hum on the map, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stotina is a little lower. Hum overlooks Mostar around here. And this is the slope that goes down to the harbour bridge, Lucki Most.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am a very precise person, Witness, so when I look at the map, I see Stotina and Hum. But before that I see Donja Mala, which is -- Donja Mahala, which is closer. That geographic area, was it covered by the BH Army to the best of your knowledge, or the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Members of the HVO held the line up to Stotina. Donja Mahala and the Bulevar were under the control of the BH Army. At Hum there were also HVO soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So at Mahala that we see here next to the river, there are houses. Would it have been technically possible for an individual, X, located in Donja Mahala, to target your house, to shoot at your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the lower part of Donja Mahala, yes. That part is called Orucluk.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are saying that it is possible from that area you indicated for a person to shoot at your terrace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I know this is a very painful testimony for you, but I would like to ask you, from Stotina where the shot could have come from to your house is an area through which the front line passed, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you show us on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can. Stotina is here, and the separation line -- shall I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you draw the separation line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The separation line was around here. It went like this. And down the Bulevar. The other side, next to the Neretva River belonged to the HVO. This side here was held by the BH Army, all the way up to the lines, to the Bulevar. All the way up to Hit and then it went down Santici Street. Whereas on this side, this whole side was in its entirety under the control of the BH Army all the way up to Santic Street to an area we call Celovina. You pass by Cernica, the Alex Santic Street, up to this area here, Celovina. All that was a line held by the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I just want to ask one last question, because the concern of this Trial Chamber is of course to know who is responsible for those tragic shootings and the intentions of those persons of course. In the vicinity of your house, were there any troops, garrison or were there any patrols? And concerning the shot that hit your wife, could you have confused the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right below my house there was the South Camp, and in the South Camp BH Army soldiers were stationed. And to confuse my wife's clothing with a uniform is absolutely impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have just brought in a new element. Every time the Judges ask a question a new element occurs. You said that around 400 metres away from you there was the South Camp of the BH Army, which raises in my mind another question, because I have to be very precise in my work. So at Stotina, was it possible to shoot from there to the side where the BH Army was at South Camp and were there any shootings from Stotina towards or targeting the South Camp of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I told you that Stotina position covered the area around my house and further up, part of the Hasan Brkic bridge and the South Camp. You could control the whole area downstream. Stotina is a hill, perhaps 30 or 40 metres high, maybe a bit higher at certain points. And it gave a very good view. The South Camp is perfectly visible. The visibility is good in all directions, towards my house and towards the South Camp. However, my house and the South Camp are at opposite sides of the hill, so if somebody were shooting at the South Camp, that bullet could certainly not stray towards my house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You have just answered, your house was not on the direct trajectory of a bullet that was directed at the South Camp from Stotina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, my house was not between the camp and Stotina. My house was to the north, 400 metres to the north. It was not in the way at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So here is one theory that we've elucidated. Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Before we go on to the videos, Witness, just a couple of final questions about what happened around the 6th of June, 1993. Is it correct, sir, that the funeral for your wife was the night of the following day, if I understood correctly, on the night between the 7th and 8th of June? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges, please, why the funeral was held at night?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the death of my wife, and I have to say the cemetery is about 50 metres away from my house, I wanted to bury her next to her father, and her father is buried in the middle of the Saric Harem which is the name of the cemetery and we had to dig the grave by night because there was shooting from up there at Hum, so we dug the grave by night and the next night we buried my wife under the cover the dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, at the time your wife's funeral whether the funeral gathering was fired on during the funeral?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we were burying my wife, there was shooting from Hum from a PAM, which is an anti-aircraft machine-gun, 12.7 millimetres, a lot of the bullets were the kind that light up the area around, so we could see where the bullets were coming from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And these bullets, which I think we could describe perhaps on what you have said including tracer rounds, how close were these shots or was this fire coming to the funeral party itself?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not so close. They fell 100 metres away from us, maybe it was an attempt to intimidate us or maybe they couldn't see us very well. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, can you just finally tell us this: Around the time that your wife was shot and killed, did you learn there were any other shootings victims in that vicinity around the same time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went the next day to Radio Mostar to ask them to announce the death of my wife and the funeral time, then I heard from the people there that somebody else had been hit in Donja Mahala, some of them were wounded or rather one woman was wounded or maybe she was killed, but anyway, someone was wounded and someone was killed. That was the information I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. If we can then please show the video. We're going to show you a videoclip, sir. It's quite short. We may need to show it -- they go rather quickly; we may have to show it more than once. It's Exhibit P 09140, and it's -- for those who want to follow the transcript -- there's a very short transcript, it's on page 2 out of 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Hadzizukic, could you, please, to the best of your recollection, indicate where you found your wife when she was shot."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, the witness seems to be looking for something, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was looking for a pencil. But I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. I apologise. Can we start the recording over, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Hadzizukic, could you, please, to the best of your recollection, indicate where you found your wife when she was shot. "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Could you please indicate on yourself where the bullet had hit your wife? "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: To the best of your recollection, could you, please, show the position in which you found the body of your wife when she was killed. "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. Now, Mr. Hadzizukic, I have an additional question with respect to this house and with respect to that house. Could you, please, tell us if these houses were there at the moment that you your wife was shot? "Witness: No. "Investigator: Thank you very much."

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I, please, have the -- could we go back now to the video where he indicated -- he pointed to his body as to the location where his wife was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: Mr. Hadzizukic, could you, please, to the best of your recollection, indicate where you found your wife when she was shot. "Witness: [Indicates] "Investigator: Thank you. Could you please indicate on yourself where the bullet had hit your wife? "Witness: [Indicates]"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, in the video now that we can see, you are pointing to a location on your head behind the right ear. Your testimony yesterday and the statement that you gave in 2001 indicates that the bullet struck your wife behind her left ear. Do you want to explain the Judges the difference between the pointing you're doing in the video and your testimony?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can. I didn't understand the question. I'm right handed by nature, so I put my right hand up and showed the place, and I didn't think it was important to show the left or the right. She was actually hit on the left side on this hard piece of bone behind the ear. But I just, as a matter of course, put my right hand up because I'm right handed. So I just wanted to show the place being behind the ear and I wasn't paying attention to whether it was left or right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could we, please, go forward then with the video and I have one more question before we leave the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: "Investigator: And to the best of your recollection, please assume the position in which you find the body of your wife when she was killed. "Witness: [Indicates]"

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can we stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday, if I heard your testimony correctly, I may have misheard, if I did I apologise, I think you may have indicated that you thought yesterday that your wife's head was facing toward the east, that is in the direction of the house. You will see that when you've given this position in the video and actually -- as described in your statement in 2001, you said the head was facing towards the west as you portray it here. I didn't want to interrupt your testimony at the end of the day yesterday, but can you clarify again that situation for us. Does this refresh your recollection that the head was facing to the west?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, she was lying the way I'm lying here on the picture. Her head was turned west towards Hum hill and Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. The next thing I'm going to show you, please, is Exhibit P 09139, which is what we call the 360-degree photograph. And what I'd like you to do, please, sir, is just watch it -- we're going to go in a full circle. Do you recall that when you were interviewed at the time that the video clip was made that we just saw that following that time the -- a tripod and a camera were placed on the spot on the terrace where your wife was killed and that a series of photographs were taken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall that after the time when you -- the -- at the time the video was taken, we saw a short video clip a moment ago. Do you recall at that time that a tripod was set up on your terrace and some additional photographs were taken?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Please look at this video. Don't make any comments initially. I'm going to make one full circle, and then I'm -- we will circle again and I will ask you a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Okay. Let's stop there for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right, sir, I'm about to start a second pass, if you will. We're going to do the same thing again. What I would like you to do, sir, please, is watch the photograph very carefully. When you see the location from which you believe that the shot came from that killed your wife, tell us to stop and I'll ask you a question or two about that. So we can start again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you indicate by looking at the photograph -- strike that. Let me start again. I think it will be simpler. If I could have the usher's assistance. Your Honour, we have made a still photo with no markings on it so the witness can make a hard copy. Sir, first of all, can you see that the photograph that's been placed on the ELMO is the same -- well, everyone in the courtroom, I suppose, can see if you change to the ELMO. That the photograph on the ELMO and the portion of the video we were looking at is roughly the same. Using the marker that the usher will provide to you, sir, on the still photograph that's on the ELMO, would you mark further the particular location from which you believe the shot came, which killed your wife.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been somewhere in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Now, first of all -- let me ask you to mark that with the number 1.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if we can have an IC number, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Madam Registrar, an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this becomes IC number 297.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I am advised, Your Honour, while I'm thinking about it, that since the earlier map was marked again, that maybe we need a second -- a different IC number for the second marking on the map. I don't know if that's true, but if it is, then we need another number.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, let's have another IC number on -- for the first map.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this becomes then IC number 298.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, you answered this question in the video, but I also wanted to ask you in the courtroom, please. The place that you have now marked on this photograph which is IC 297, the building that you have marked, you have made a red circle roughly on a house about in the middle of the picture. Was that house at that location in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: There is another house or -- that's even closer to us just off the connected, in fact -- virtually connected to the terrace there. Was that house at that location in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges, approximately, as best you can, when those two buildings were built?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These houses were built almost at the same time; four, five, six years ago, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have a question looking at the photograph. Behind the two newly-built houses, I see a white building with windows. There are apparently three floors to the building. And from the terrace, one has the impression that that building over there is a little higher up. In 1993, in the month of June, was that other building there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that building, was it in the BH Army zone or the HVO zone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was under BH Army control.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in June 1993, perhaps you know this or not, what was in the building? Was it a residential building? What kind of building was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was a residential building with tenants.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, if I can ask you, please, you've made a marking before on the top of the circle which might be interpreted as a one, maybe you intended it to be a 1, but can I just, please, ask you to mark somewhere around that circle again something that's clearly a number 1.

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to finish then very briefly with two exhibits. And perhaps the usher can help you while he's there. If I can just ask you to look ever so briefly at Exhibit 2655. It's in the bundle there. Can you just confirm to us, sir, is this a death certificate issued by a hospital in Mostar concerning the -- the death of your wife?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. That is the death certificate which was signed by a lady doctor, Dr. Posic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And can I ask you to go to the next exhibit. If you just go in the bundle to 9131. Can you just confirm to the Judges that this is a further record concerning the death of your wife on the 6th of June, 1993, an extract record made from the register of deaths?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. Yes, that is the register of deaths and the extract about my wife's death.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you will please look at the -- before we finish, if you will just please look at the date on the lower left corner of the Bosnian-language version of the document, just so there is no confusion. utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, the Prosecution has no further questions. Sir, I want to thank you once again for coming to The Hague to give your evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Let's start off with the cross-examination. With respect to the visit of the UN Secretary-General, we are going to take a break at 10.00 and resume at 10.30. In the next 10 minutes, who wishes to start off? Council Tomic. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have no questions for this Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Next Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have given our time to the Praljak Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. We have no questions for this gentleman. We wish to thank him for coming to give his evidence. Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. We have no questions and we are prepared to give our time to General Praljak should he require it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the order, Mr. Praljak has a few questions for the witness and perhaps I would have two or three additional questions after that. Thank you.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak, how much time do you need for your questions? I know that usually you ask very specific and precise questions. So how much time do you need? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I don't think I'll be able to get through them by 10.00. I'd like to show a few photographs to make things clearer to the Trial Chamber and everybody else in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Go ahead. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, my screen isn't working, the monitor isn't working here, but I will begin nonetheless. Cross-examination by the Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: You have to understand that it is very difficult for me to ask you questions, to have to ask you questions, but unfortunately I do have to do that in order to clarify the situation as much as is possible. It would be better if somebody else could answer the questions, but there we have it. May we have on the ELMO, Mr. Usher...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Usher, please. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can start off with some other questions. Tell me, please, Witness, an M 48 rifle, was that the standard type of weapon that the Yugoslav People's Army had?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it a 7.9 millimetre calibre rifle?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the rifle was a 7.62 calibre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We're not going to debate the issue. But tell me, does it fire individually so that it's not a semi-automatic rifle or an automatic rifle, but you have to repeat and fire each individual time?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, could anybody buy that kind of rifle before the war and during the war, if they had the money? Did things like that happen, that people bought these kind of rifles?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And very often was it hunters that bought rifles of this kind with a Zeiss optic sight or whatever and used it as a hunting carbine?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult up to the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: How about after the war and during the war?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably easier then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So I think you and I agree on this point that that kind of weapon, not only that weapon, but especially this particular weapon, could be purchased and procured relatively easily on the market, both before the war and in the war itself; is that correct? That anybody could buy this kind of rifle if they had a few hundred German marks, right before the war, let's say?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was difficult to do that before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't mean before the conflicts began, but when the Yugoslav Peoples' Army came to Mostar, when the reservists came, when the clashes and conflicts started, could you buy an M 48 rifle from a reservist, for example?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was difficult to buy one from a reservists. I don't know of anybody buying them from reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, can we take a look at a photograph, but before that, tell me, please, was it possible to control regardless of what you knew to control who had a rifle? We know that many people purchased a rifle and kept them at home. Was it possible to control this procurement of rifles, left, right anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spent the -- the whole war in Mostar, and lots of things happened in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now we have the photograph on our screens. Would you look at it. I have been told that I did not get an answer to my question. That is to say whether there were individual shots from the rifle and whether you had to cock the rifle each time you wanted to shoot?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did give an answer. And yes, you had to repeat and cock the rifle every time you wanted to shoot from this M 48 rifle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. It doesn't seem to have been recorded but it is now. Now, on this aerial photograph here, we can see Stotina, Hasan Brkic bridge, and according to what I know, this is how the area under BH army control looked like, what the deployment was like. It is in the grey-green colour. Is what I have just said correct? Would you agree with what I have said?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Then on the photograph, would you put a number 1 for the area that is in the greenish colour and put a 1 there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Right. So that is the area controlled by the BH Army. And the left area, the darker area, could you put a number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. And draw a circle around these houses at Stotina, the houses we can see, that's Stotina, I think. Draw a circle around that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All this is Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Right. That's right. And put a number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this is a small cafe over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Put 3 on Stotina.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now -- can we now -- or rather, can I have an IC number, Your Honours, for this photograph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My house would be somewhere in this area over here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where you've drawn the dot, all right. Put a number 4 by your house then, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you just put ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An IC number, please.

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Place your initials on the document, please, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. May we have the next photograph, please. That's the same general area, but broader. So on this broader area, would you once again put where the BH Army was and put a number 1 for the BH Army, the HVO positions 2, please. And Stotina, number 3?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My house is exactly located on this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Right. Thank you. Would you put your initials there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] And may we have an IC number, please.

utterances.text: [Marks] THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: While you are doing that, would you mark the South Camp.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI

utterances.text: Mr. President, excuse me for interrupting. I apologise to Mr. Praljak. Before we leave it Your Honour, just so the record is clear, we broke looking at IC 300, which was a map of -- and I just want the record to be very clear, and I don't want to have to come back to it later. Could we see IC 300 for a moment? Thank you. Thank you, Usher. I apologise. Mr. President, I just, in reviewing the transcript just now, I just want it to be very clear that when the witness said that the South Camp was there, the record just says there. That when we look at IC 300, the witness was indicating that it was off the photograph, somewhere down in the lower left on the lower left side. The South Camp is not shown in this photograph at all. I just wanted the record to be clear. Thank you. Sorry, Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct. And after that Mr. Praljak did not wish to inquire further into the location of the South Camp. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I will not discuss this with this witness, but we see the edge of the South Camp on this photograph. We will have other maps later.

utterances.text: Witness, we see a photograph of Hum overlooking Mostar, and the line of separation between the HVO and the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina is marked. utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 301. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Next photograph, please. I would like the witness to look at the map on his right-hand side, the large map, where red marks, what we have seen before, separation lines between the HVO along Hasan Brkic bridge, then it crosses over Donja Mahala to the foot of the Hum hill, and from the Hasan Brkic bridge the separation line was to the right, the Neretva river; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We will put numbers later. Can you mark 1 for the top of Hum hill.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Will you also mark Stotina with number 2. From Hasan Brkic bridge to the right. Put a 2 there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Please, you say that you saw the bunkers made by the HVO, and can you now show on the map what it is that you saw. Put a number 3, if you remember where it was.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Did you write number 3? Behind the red line, could you write ABH and write HVO where the HVO was.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And on that map, can you try to locate your house, put a number 4, let's say.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to mark it exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Number 4, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 302. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I have only a couple more photographs that I would like placed on the ELMO to clarify this completely. Is this Stotina? You see the road. Is that the group of houses at Stotina?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could you put a circle around them and number 1. Draw a circle around all of the houses at Stotina. Number 1.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, in this photograph, will you draw the -- mark the location of the bunker.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. It was not a bunker; it was a fortification of sandbags along this whole line. It's a steep slope, a cliff practically, below, and they made fortifications to protect these houses. It was on the edge.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well. Put your initials there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And an IC number, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 303. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: We see Stotina here and the house that we saw before. And the place where you showed those sandbags were placed along the edge here of the cliff. Can you mark that, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And put a number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And those houses down below, were they already under the control of the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were constantly under the control of the BH Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: At that time, to the best of your recollection, were there troops and residents alike, or were the troops around the houses and residents inside?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, don't ask me that. There were probably people from the BH Army who lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Put your initials there, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So number 2 is the BH Army. IC number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR

utterances.text: This is a photograph provided by the Prosecutor, and this red stain marks certain houses at Stotina. Do you see this red stain?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]

utterances.text: Less than a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Six steps? How many centimetres?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are probably the standard 18 centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: So approximately 90 centimetres. I made a mistake in drawing this sketch because I drew a fence, but on the photograph we saw those boxes with flowers. Were they there at the time or did you put them up later?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can you just draw on this line -- on this picture where the bullet came from?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the house, and this is one terrace, I don't see where you drew the steps. My wife was here. The bullet came from this side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Place a number 2 for the bullet. And number 2, the position of your wife.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And your initials.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, you hear this theory that the bullet came from there, but if we imagine for a moment that another theory is possible, based on the position of the slippers on steps 3 and 1, would it have been possible for her to be hit while she was climbing the steps? Would it have changed the trajectory of the bullet? Because the theory that we have to take into account was that she was struck by a bullet at the moment when she was climbing down the stairs, and that she was hit where she was hit in the head, and she lost her slippers on the steps, and you found her at the bottom of the stairs. Would that have changed the trajectory of the bullet, as you believe it to be.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, when my wife went outside, she stayed there one or two minutes. We had a cat and she was talking to that cat. I heard her. She stayed there for a while, so she could not have been hit while she was moving. She was still, standing still.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are three possibilities. She was hit at the moment when she was talking to the cat before the steps. Second possibility, she was climbing down the steps when she was hit. And three, she was hit by a bullet when she was at the bottom of the stairs. What is your opinion, your estimate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My opinion is that she was hit while she was standing down there, talking to the cat, and I think she was hit then. That's my opinion, based on where the wound was, and where I found the slippers and which way the slippers were facing. That's my belief. Of course, nobody knows what exactly happened. There is nobody who will prove that. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] IC number, please, for this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 307. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: This is the last sketch. The stairs are obviously too big. I didn't know how many there were. Can you draw on this sketch from which direction the bullet came.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From this direction. My wife was lying here. Rather, on this -- on this terrace. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Cross out what you drew first, put a number 1.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And your initials.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, from this sketch, where is the cat here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't see the cat. I suppose she was down there. Because animals have instincts and maybe she had a premonition. It was a very nice, gentle cat, and she lived in my house. And for three days then, she had not come into the house, and I heard the conversation between my wife and this cat and my wife was saying, "Cicko, why aren't you coming into the house?" I have a little terrace down here, two or three square metres. You saw it on the photograph. We used it for storage, and I suppose it was underneath.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the pen you have, by placing the pen vertically, could you show us on this sketch the position of your wife when she was hit by a bullet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I got out I found two slippers. Here. One here and one on the first step. I found her lying there. I believe the cat was underneath the terrace from all I saw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But if your wife was standing at the place -- on the spot where you found her lying, how do you explain the fact that her slippers were higher, were above her?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I have seen a lot of traffic accidents where the victims lost whatever they were wearing on their feet. I found her slippers there and I believe that she lost them. She had a bruise by her cheek bone and everything indicates that she was turned that way judging by the place where her slippers were, the wound behind her left ear. So that's my opinion and what I'm convinced of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I apologise once again for having to ask you these questions, but the slippers that you marked there, can you put a number 2 by them. 2 for slippers.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And number 3 where you think the cat was.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And tell me, please, this is very important, if you can remember at all. The position of the slippers, were you able to conclude that your late wife was climbing up the stairs or coming down the stairs?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that most probably she was standing and talking to the cat, and she was standing and hit standing and that her slippers fell off her feet. That is my opinion, and I stand by that opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Witness, I am not trying in any way, and please understand this, in any way to influence what you are saying. Please understand me when I say that. But what I'm saying is regardless of whether she was standing or coming down the steps, judging by the position of the slippers, was she facing the stairs as if she were climbing up the -- going to climb up the stairs or climbing up the stairs or away from the stairs climbing down?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found her lying down. I was on the settee in the room. I was inside, so I didn't see whether she was actually standing, standing still or moving around. Only God can know things like that. So don't make me say things that I don't know. I can't actually know what happened. But it is my opinion that she was standing still at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, without trying to be Sherlock Holmes, there is a point on which there can be no discussion, and that is you said that the bullet hit her under her left ear. Now, this fact excludes her having been hit when she was going up the stairs because if she was going up the stairs and hit then, then the bullet would have entered through her right ear, not her left ear. So she cannot have been going up the stairs. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think the same as you have just said. I think she was standing. That's why I say she was standing, because she was facing Stotina with her left side. So if she was hit behind her left ear, then it was that side of her face or head that was facing Stotina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry to interrupt and I only do so in the interests of ensuring that nothing is missed here. I should point out to the Trial Chamber and to everyone in court that on Prosecution Exhibit 02655, which is the -- a medical report dealing with the death of the witness's wife, there is a reference in Latin which appears to be the abbreviation DEX, which is presumably an abbreviation for Dexter, meaning right, and the reference is to the skull. There was some confusion that Mr. Scott tried to clear up when the witness, on the video, was indicating with his right hand on the right part of his skull when asked to demonstrate the point of entry. And he later clarified that by saying that he was right handed, but it might be a matter which the Trial Chamber thinks could be inquired into further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Witness, the certificate describing the circumstances of the death of your wife, in the B/C/S document that you have in front of you, there are some Latin words, and the last word there is osccp. Dx. The osccp might be occiput. I don't know about the X, but the Defence is saying right, which seems to indicate that the wound was on the right and not on the left. Are you sure that the bullet hit your wife above the left ear, behind the left ear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you 100 per cent certain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because the wound, the shock that you had -- well, did you look at the wound up close? Did you have a close look at wound?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and my daughter was with me, she was 15 years old at the time. I don't wish to -- I don't want to recall any other sights. My daughter suffered worse than I did. I saw the wound when we brought my wife into the house, and I saw that around the wound there was brain matter splattered, white pieces of brain matter splattered and very little blood. And as time passed, my wife was in the house for 15 minutes or half an hour before she was taken to the mortuary was very hot, warm. I held my wife. I took her into the house. I saw her. So can you please spare me any further details. We've been discussing this for three days now. I think I've had enough. I can't take anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we volunteer this? Mr. Murphy very helpfully offered some learning. It is very difficult to decide for everything, but a couple of the words are very clear. Second line in the Bosnian, the B/C/S version of the death certificate is capitis, which is of the head. And the last two words seem to be protrusio or protrusio and then cerebra, that clearly is a reference to brain. So it looks as if the last line there is referring to the effects on the brain. Your Honour, the suggestion is that because the English translation is plainly not complete and there has been a difficulty with legibility, that this particular item should be sent for translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we shall request a translation of that from the CLSS. Yes, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart makes the point that I was about to rise and make. And with all respect to those who know more about Latin in the courtroom than I do, I really don't think we should be speculating too much about it. Mr. Murphy may indeed be 100 per cent right, but the obvious solution is to ask that the language be fully translated. Having said that, Your Honour, the witness has made it quite clear and was quite adamant that the wound was on the left side. While I'm on my feet, Your Honour, I think, I must make the record on these various sketches that Mr. Praljak has prepared, apparently in his own hand. They are not to scale. I appreciate that he has made some effort, but there is no indication that they are accurate or to scale. He has shown a number of these drawings to the witness very quickly. The witness has not really had a chance to see these before coming in the courtroom or give them much thought. Some of these markings are being made very quickly on drawings that are not to scale and not necessarily properly oriented. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Praljak, I personally consider that the sketches allow the witness to show us what happened, so although they are maybe not to scale, they are there so we have them and we will take note of that. We still have three witnesses to get through, so do you have any more questions? THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I have almost finished, and I apologise to the witness, I won't go back to this area. I said that these sketches were not to scale and asked the witness about the various levels and heights.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Anyway, Witness, I'm not going to go on about that. Just two more questions. You said that you saw a bunker at Hum being blown up. Obviously someone from the BH Army side had hit it and it was blown up. On that big map to your right, where were the BH Army artillery positions? Because you can't raze a bunker to the ground or up in the air with an ordinary bullet, you have to use artillery weapons.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a ZIS canon being brought and I know that the first shell or bullet hit half a metre below the window and the other one hit the bunker and the shooting went on for three hours. This was something that was talked about in Mostar. It was an event that people talked about and people were very pleased that the shot was successful.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: What about the ZIS position?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bukvic house on -- and my house, it was in between. It was halfway between my house and the Bukvic house. So everything we saw was from the west side. My house is on the east side on the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And the Zeiss was behind your house, was it?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there was my house, then another house that we saw there, and then the wall of the third house, so it was behind that wall. I will try and show you. If this is Marsal Tito Street, I can tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Look at it on the large map.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't see anything on that big map. We said that this was the bridge. So if this is the Neretva and I said that my house was here, then Marsal Tito Street is here, which curves down by the cafe, everybody knows the cafe there, and then you go to Mejdan. Behind Bukvic's house, which is the third house after my house, that's where the ZIS resist cannon was shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Would you place the ZIS above that position.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: My last question: In June when this happened, when this killing or when your wife was hit, in Mostar on the left bank, were the civilian authorities functioning, the civilian police for instance or some other civilian services, the courts, were they working? Were the civilian authorities functioning?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really don't remember. I know that something was organised in the local community, some sort of civil government, civilian government. There were soldiers as well. Everything went on at the same time just as it did on the opposite side.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Now, my very last question. When you reported the death of your wife, did anybody make what we call an on-site investigation? Did they call for an investigation, either then or after the war or during the war? Was there an on-site investigation on the scene of the crime into your wife's killing?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely no.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness, and I apologise for having to ask you those questions. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't seem to have given an IC number for the last sketch, the one we still have up on our screens. Madam Registrar, an IC number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be IC number 308.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I think that Mr. Praljak has asked all the questions. Mr. Kovacic, do you have any additional ones then?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, just two very short questions to round off this topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, the bunker that you were asked about that exploded when it was hit by a Zeiss at Stotina, can you tell us what time of day that was?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at Hum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes, Hum.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the afternoon. I can't give you an exact time, but sometime in the afternoon around 5.00 or 6.00 roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And the date?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the date, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Could you say if it was spring, autumn?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And a moment ago, and there's something about that in your statement, you say that on the same day when your wife was killed there were two other female victims. Do you know where they fell victim, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about that when I went to Mostar and they said that two other women fell casualty at Donja Mahala, that one was killed and the other was wounded. Now, whether that was that day or the following day, well, I went the following day. So that's when I heard about it. So it might have been that day or --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear their names that day or later on?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I really didn't because there were a lot of people that were killed in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart, any relevant and useful questions from you?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, we have no questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Re-examination. Useful and relevant?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, if I could.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could have the usher's assistance to put before the witness IC 303, 304, and 305. And if you want to have IC 297 at hand as well, that would be helpful. If I can, first, ask the witness to be shown on the ELMO, 303, IC 303.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, at the very -- to the left -- excuse me. On the photograph to the right of the number 1 and just on the top edge of the circle you drew, do you see a house there on the top of the hill? Or a structure?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can see this building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't see what you're pointing at. Can you do it on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Could I ask you to put -- mark that with a number 2, the building at the top of the hill. Excuse me, there is a number 2 already. 3. Please mark it -- change it to a 3. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I can't see the number 2. With that in mind, sir, can you then please go to IC 304. And can you tell the Judges whether you can see what -- the same structure you just marked on the top of Stotina, appears to you? If you can see it.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know what number we are up to on that. Looks like we have a number 4 already. Could I ask you to -- number 5, please.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Number 5 on the house, please. Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: And if I could ask you, please, to look at IC 305. I'm sorry, 305 I think is another photo if I'm not mistaken. I believe it's IC 305. Can we just confirm for the record that that's -- that we're now looking at IC 305? Is that right? 302? All right. I'm informed we are now looking at IC 302. Sir, can you look again at that photo and can you see the same house or structure that we've been looking at in the last two photos and if you see that one, let me ask you to mark it number 5.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. Thank you very much. Sir, can I ask that -- can I ask the usher to assist you in looking at IC 297. Sir, is that a photograph -- we marked that before, but what we're looking at in terms of Mr. Praljak's sketches, is that an angle looking from the steps going down from the upper terrace to the lower terrace and then looking back roughly to the southwest. First of all, is that the terrace showing the upper terrace and then the step the -- a handrail, a rail we can see in the foreground of the picture going down to the -- or being on the second or lower terrace?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the upper terrace. These are the steps leading down to the entrance gate of the yard. This is the lower terrace, and these are the steps. You can't see them here, but they go down to this railing and the entrance into the yard. And the other steps were over here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: All right. We have to be very clear for the record, sir, because you've made -- jumped around the photo and made a number of markings. When you point to the lower left corner of the photograph, going where the stairs are leaning downward, going off the photograph, does that go down to the entrance to your apartment?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entrance to my yard is down here. And the entrance to my flat, to my house is up here, over here. So the first level terrace and the second level terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. When I say the entry to your apartment, coming into your property from the outside is at an access point at the bottom of the stairs leading off the picture to the right; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This is the entrance to my yard, to my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Is it correct to say, sir, that the photo we're looking at now, if one were to be standing looking -- standing at the very bottom of this photograph and looking toward what you've marked as number 1, would one be standing on what you've called the lower terrace?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand. Where am I standing?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If you're standing in the very beginning of the -- exactly from where the perspective from where this photograph is taken, you see that you -- you see the rail there in front of you?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the photograph was taken from the first terrace, the smaller terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: The lower terrace, can we also use the term lower terrace in reference to the upper terrace?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you can say that. This picture was taken from the lower terrace, the smaller, lower terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there are six steps leading down to that lower, smaller terrace, or to the entrance, six steps to the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... usher's assistance and if I could have a number for the next IC number please, the next -- the new IC number. A brand new IC number, whatever the next is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For which photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: A new photograph, Your Honour. It's a still from the video. I just need a number for reference purposes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but I would like to see it on the screen to see which one it is. So you want a number for that one there?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have an IC number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is IC number 309.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Just for the record, sir, can you just -- can you just confirm that those are the steps leading down, rather than having Mr. Praljak's sketches which are not to scale, can you agree that those are the steps leading down from the upper terrace to the lower terrace.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the upper terrace. These are the steps leading down to the smaller terrace, and then from that lower terrace the steps go further down westward to the entrance into the yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Sir, can I ask you to mark once again please on this photograph the steps where, as best you can recall, your wife's slippers were found.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD HADZIZUKIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would make it here. And the lower one. Is this the first one? If that's the first one, then that would be the third. Or if there is one other step below this photograph, then -- I think the first and the third anyway. I can't see whether there's -- I'll cross that middle one out then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I have another question which isn't directly related to the slippers. On the white wall that we can see there I see some spots. Now, I asked myself two questions, having seen them: Are they damp marks or were they holes caused by shells or bullets which were later on filled in with plaster or cement or whatever? And which appear that way. The spots, is that from the damp or is there another reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Those smudges or spots are the remainders of the projectiles of snipers. I filled in those holes, losing -- using a little gypsum, white wash and so on. I was going to paint over the facade, but it's still like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, there we have it then. So what you are telling us is that on the wall that we can see there in the photograph, your wall bears the traces of shell impacts, bullet impacts shot by the sniper.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are sniper shots and also projectiles --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At what time? Before June, after June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Up until my wife's death, there was not much shooting, so these are probably the remains of what happened afterwards. Because afterwards we were on the right bank. When I returned to my house, because I was expelled from my house, I found these marks on the wall.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm going to count with you. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14 smudges or spots which can correspond to 14 impact points. Now, each of these smudges, was there a hit from a projectile and that afterwards you plastered over the holes, filled them in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two projectiles were fired at my house; my roof was damaged. And the front, north side of my house, the north wall, there is a half metre hole where what I believe was a small shell impacted on the attic. And on that side, from that side here, the south side, this other house had not been built yet, another shell fell. And around the house, I cannot count how many shells had fallen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the floor that we are looking at now, these stains, do they have anything to do with projectiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you mark the spots that you filled in, that you plastered over, from what you recollect?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All these spots that you can see, all of those are repairs and there were bigger holes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Show us with the pen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All of these spots. I repaired them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So all these filled in holes, from which area did the bullets come? What was their trajectory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Either from Hum or from Stotina, all of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And these shots happened after June, after the death of your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: If I could ask the witness to be shown, I think, what was IC 308. And could the witness still leave, please, Exhibit -- still leave IC 297 there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
