utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the Defence can call that witness, of course, in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I have just one more short question for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: You said in your statement and you partially confirmed that today that at the hospital you spent about three months because of the wounding. Now, when you were leaving the hospital, did you receive any medical records or documentation, some letter of discharge or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps my father did because my father came to fetch me. I should have stayed on a little longer in the hospital, but I wanted to go home. I couldn't take it anymore. I know it was late at night when my father came to fetch me and he said, "Why don't you stay another night, stay for tonight." And I said, "I can't." So then we left together. And I can't remember if he took the discharge papers or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: So you are saying you don't know?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: That's right. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the investigators in 2001, when you talked to them and gave the statement and in 2004 the reconstruction when it was filmed, did anyone ask you whether you had any medical records, discharge papers or whatever?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: I can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No more questions. I have completed my cross-examination. Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, when your friend's father parked the vehicle on the occasion you described, did he park right outside the building where he was to go and do work on a sewer pipe?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: He parked in front of the building and I think he was supposed to do work behind the building because we didn't see him. He went off somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And then you have mentioned the Volkswagen Golf. What was the distance between the truck that you were in and the Volkswagen Golf vehicle when they were both parked?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't tell you exactly, but one and a half to two metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And it was the front of the Volkswagen vehicle, was it, that was facing -- was nearest to the front of the truck you were in? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So then the alternative then is that you say both vehicles were facing in the same direction? That's right?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you were behind, to get it absolutely clear, your truck was behind the Volkswagen vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And of course the driver got out, as you have described. You said in your statement, and you mentioned a few minutes ago that you had to sit close together and the driver had complained, as drivers often do about small boys, that he didn't have enough room. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: While driving, he complained while driving, while we were on our way there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: This is what we are coming to. It was a bench seat, wasn't it? It was a bench seat all across the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: I think there were just two seats next to the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: All right. Your statement says you had to sit close together on the small bench next to the driver's seat, right. When the driver got out you had a bit more space, so did you -- did you spread yourselves a bit and move over?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. We did a bit. We played around a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: So you would have moved over towards the left, in the direction you were facing, you would have spread yourself a bit, move yourself a more comfortable, move over to the left. That's obvious, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. We pushed around a bit. I can't everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Already. Now you said you heard the sound of a second flying bullet. That is in your statement. Have we got it right this morning when you talked about seeing fire in the window, you appeared to be talking about that second shot. Is that understanding correct?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: In your statement you say that you heard the sound of a second flying bullet, "And I saw that this bullet impacted in either the motor hood or front windshield of the yellow Volkswagen Golf. This second shot appeared to be in the direct line with the first shot." And you say, "I remember that I said to my friend something like, look, the car in front of us is hit and it is moving closer to us." So are you saying that you made those observations about the second bullet and where it hit on the ground, made those comments to your friend and also saw the fire in the window connected with that shot? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Well, we talked about it in the truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: You see, I'm going to put, because the tradition I come from involves putting things fairly and squarely. I'm going to put to you that this is not true. You did not see any fire in a window, and that this is a new idea that you have produced today. What do you say?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: What do you want me to say? What can I say? You can think --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... would like you to say the truth, which is what I'm inviting you to do. This is your chance to answer the question under solemn declaration as truthfully as possible. Let me make it clear. I am saying that you have produced this for the first time and it is not true that you saw fire from a window on that day.

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: We did see this flash. I remember talking about it in the truck. We said, "Look, that's where the shooting is coming from." I can't remember everything, I was a child after all, but I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... that you saw the flash now? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: We said to each other, "Look at that, there's shooting." We found it strange, unusual.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Okay. Let's get back to -- do you say you saw the flash?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you saw the flash and you saw the bullet hit the road between you and the Volkswagen vehicle? That's what you say, do you?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: I don't know about this vehicle in between the Golf and us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No I'm not suggesting any vehicle, let's not get confused. Maybe there is a translation or maybe we're going too fast. Let's get it clear. According to you there was a gap between your truck and the Volkswagen vehicle. That's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And you saw three bullets, one impacted on the surface of the road between the two vehicles. That's right, is it? That's the first one. It's what your statement says.

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: And the second one you say in your statement -- we read this before, but it impacted in either the motor hood or the front windshield. Right?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: The way you have described the vehicles parked, that was at the far end of the Volkswagen vehicle, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. But you can see this from a height, because the truck was high up. So you could see this.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not necessarily questioning that. Just make it clear. You personally, and I'm distinguishing you from your friend, you saw those things, the first bullet hitting the surface of the road, the second bullet hitting the vehicle. You saw both those things yourself, correct?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to end there. Mr. Bos.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just one clarification, because the record now doesn't read the way it was, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness, the first bullet, where did the first bullet impact on the street? Was this in front of the Volkswagen or on the -- behind the Volkswagen?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: In front of the Volkswagen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir, for -- ah, we have people on their feet. Mr. Petkovic, quickly. The Judges have received enough information, so go ahead, if you must. Cross-examination by the Accused Petkovic: THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] I would like to ask the witness how he was able to see the bullet hit the ground.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] How shall I explain that? I just saw dust on the road. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: And at what time did the shot come during the day?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Between 4.00 and 5.00. I can't be more exact.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Did you ever shoot from a rifle during the day in your life?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Yes, when I was in the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Can you see a flash during the day when you shoot from a rifle during the day?

utterances.speaker: ANEL HELJIC
utterances.text: Not during the day, but the room was dark. THE ACCUSED PETKOVIC: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Witness, for coming. I'm going to ask the usher to escort you out of the courtroom. Mr. Mundis, as far as next week is concerned, before the expert witness comes in, we have four more witnesses to hear who were victims. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. That is, in fact, correct. I -- hopefully we'll be able to get through those four witnesses as expeditiously as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I did, at the end of the last break, circulate a more complete trial schedule for the month of February, and I will point out that we've completed that and filled out the rest of the month of February in terms of witnesses and I will also point out that one of the witnesses that was previously scheduled whose name I'm not going to say in public, that witness has now been rescheduled or will be rescheduled. His name has been taken off the -- for the month of February, but we anticipate calling him at a later point in time, due to some scheduling conflicts. So I have circulated a new schedule and we will call the next two scheduled sniping witnesses at the commencement of the hearing on Monday to be followed by the two that are listed for Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. MURPHY
utterances.text: Your Honour, very briefly. May I have just a few seconds on a procedural matter. Your Honour, the Prosecution has filed some objections to documents tendered by the Stojic Defence which were put to the witness Jovan Rajkov. Your Honour, we do intend to file a brief response. Due to the fact that I was out of town for a couple of days, may I have one more day to do that and file it by tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because you were absent, yes, if you would like. One more day. Ms. Tomic, you were on your feet a number of times. MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was on my feet because our turn was to cross-examine the witness next, and we had one or two questions, but I didn't -- it never came to me because things turned out the way they did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Counsel Tomic, I thought -- well, for the transcript, can you tell us which questions you wanted to ask the witness? MS. TOMASEGOVIC TOMIC: [Interpretation] I wanted to follow on from what Mr. Murphy said and ask a question with respect to when the witness saw the truck for the first time. Because it turns out that he saw the truck three or four years after the incident and then looked at the truck. So I was interested in hearing who took him to the location, whether the truck was in the location and when he looked over the truck. And after, I think it was Mr. Stewart's examination or Mr. Petkovic, this gave rise to another question, because the witness said that the room was dark from where the flash had come. And I think that's a very interesting question. If it was dark in the cabin he was in, as in terms of visibility and so on, that he explained it in that way. Because we don't know what room he had in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are going to bear in mind the questions that you had the intention to ask, but unfortunately did not have a chance to. So he is going to have to come back on Monday at 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 5th day of February, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.51 p.m.,
